newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: GDP revisions show more NZ internal growth - ANZ.
newsitem.headline: GDP revisions show more NZ internal growth - ANZ.

text.p: Statistics New Zealand's revisions of its quarterly expenditure on GDP series reinforce the view that internal demand has significantly outpaced growth in the external sector recently, ANZ bank said on Monday.
ANZ economists said that SNZ had undertaken extensive revisions of the series in releasing provisional annual national accounts, on November 11, for the year ended March 1996.

The revisions had not been publicised or explained at the time but ANZ understood they were part of SNZ's ongoing efforts to explain, and where necessary correct for, the continued divergences between the production GDP series (GDPP) and the

"SNZ commented that they have now exhausted most avenues for correcting the deficiencies in the GDPE series. Nevertheless, we would caution users of the GDPE series, which remains rather more volatile than GDPP," ANZ said.
"As a result of the changes, GDPE growth since 1993 is now higher than previously estimated although it is currently lagging growth in GDPP."

The changes in the GDPE series produced a more plausible track for aggregate activity than the old series and reinforced "the widely held view that internal demand has significantly outpaced growth in the external sector in recent times", the bank said.
"Whilst strong employment growth has helped to buoy consumption, so too has continued very strong growth in household borrowing. --Wellington Newsroom (64 4) 4734746
